title: 4.5 DeMoivre's Theorem

icans: I can use DeMoivre's Theorem to raise a complex number to a power.
I can find the nth roots of a complex number.
I can solve equations like x³ = 1 using roots of complex numbers.

vocab: nth root of a complex number

blocks.p: Multiply the long way. Then compare with 1 + i = √2(cos π/4 + i sin π/4).

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: DeMoivre's Theorem: [r(cos θ + i sin θ)]ⁿ = _______________(cos nθ + i sin nθ)
nth roots: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) has exactly n distinct nth roots: ⁿ√r[cos((θ + 2πk)/n) + i sin((θ + 2πk)/n)], k = 0, 1, …, _______________.
Spacing: the nth roots lie on a circle, equally spaced _______________ apart.

blocks.stem: Find the cube roots of −2 + 2i. Round to four decimal places.
